Literature-informed modification: The statement balances a weak near-term macro outlook with strong policy support. The Fed’s commitment to average 2% inflation and to keep the funds rate at 0–0.25% until realized outcomes improve is consistent with New Keynesian policy design and Taylor-rule-style guidance that call for stronger responses when inflation persistently undershoots target (Clarida–Galí–Gertler; Taylor rule references). At the effective lower bound, increasing Treasury and agency MBS holdings operates through the term-structure and credit channels to compress longer-term yields and sustain market functioning, consistent with research that the Federal Reserve can influence long-term rates and the slope of the yield curve and with the credit channel emphasized in the finance literature (Bernanke–Gertler; Federal Reserve influences on long-term rates and financial conditions). Implementation via interest on reserves and overnight reverse repos reflects a floor system consistent with modern central bank operating procedures. These actions help anchor longer-run inflation expectations around 2%, supporting credibility highlighted in the monetary policy literature (Goodfriend; Walsh).

Net tone: Despite continued recovery, the statement stresses that activity and employment remain well below earlier levels and that the public health crisis poses considerable risks—negatives that outweigh, but are partially offset by, highly accommodative policy and credible forward guidance. On balance, slightly negative.
